description: Rules for treating an online comment forum as a common-pool resource, as discussed in the Republik dialogue of September 2026: a free monthly word allowance, an exponential fee above it so that the affordable volume is bounded whatever the commenter's wealth, an additional sort by least attention, and a monthly reset. Worked examples with four commenter profiles and two budgets. Parameters and example numbers are assumed; the argumentation carries confidence values. Includes the dispute whether deliberate overuse or a self-set limit better serves the rule. Version 0.0.2 adds a Fermi estimate per rule: yearly benefit, effort and harm in US dollars for three adoption scenarios (20, 50 and 80 percent of internet users on adopting sites), with leakage of the effect to non-adopting platforms and a platform count that grows steeply with coverage. All Fermi inputs are assumed and carry confidence values; the results are stored and verified by calc-validation.

triples.name: comment forum
triples.description: The reader discussion area of an online publication; here the Republik dialogue.

triples.name: word count
triples.description: Number of words a commenter publishes in a period.

triples.name: free allowance
triples.description: Number of comment words per period that cost nothing beyond the subscription.

triples.name: excess words
triples.description: Comment words above the free allowance in a period.

triples.name: doubling step
triples.description: Number of excess words after which the fee doubles.

triples.name: doubling count
triples.description: How many doubling steps the excess words span.

triples.name: base fee
triples.description: Fee charged for the first doubling step.

triples.name: comment fee
triples.description: Fee for comment words above the free allowance; grows exponentially with the excess.

triples.name: Republik subscription price
triples.description: Regular yearly membership price of Republik.

triples.name: reader attention
triples.description: Time and focus readers spend on the forum; every extra comment consumes some of it.

triples.name: publisher cost
triples.description: Money the publisher spends on hosting, moderating and storing comments.

triples.name: storage cost
triples.description: Cost of keeping comments available; grows as long as nothing is ever deleted.

triples.name: exclusion cost
triples.description: Cost of preventing non-authorized persons from using the resource; defining criterion of a common-pool resource.

triples.name: common-pool resource
triples.description: Resource system with high subtractability of use and high cost of exclusion; a property of the good, not of its ownership.

triples.name: tragedy of the commons
triples.description: Hardin's 1968 model of inevitable degradation; it assumes open access, which is why Ostrom regarded the label as a misnomer.

triples.name: design principle
triples.description: Regularity found in long-enduring self-governed common-pool resource institutions; diagnostic, not a recipe.

triples.name: graduated sanctions
triples.description: Fifth of Ostrom's design principles: users who violate rules receive sanctions that escalate with the seriousness and repetition of the offence.

triples.name: comment forum as common-pool resource
triples.description: Claim of the dialogue: the forum costs every reader time and the publisher money, so it is subtractable and hard to fence; an allocation problem, not a disinformation problem.

triples.name: storage adds to publisher cost
triples.description: Because comments are stored without end, the resource use of a comment keeps growing after it is written.

triples.name: attention concentration
triples.description: Share of reader attention captured by the few most visible comments.

triples.name: popular sort
triples.description: Existing Republik dialogue sort option: most popular first.

triples.name: reply sort
triples.description: Existing Republik dialogue sort option: most replies first.

triples.name: unnoticed sort
triples.description: Proposed additional sort option: comments with the least attention first.

triples.name: allowance rule
triples.description: Rule 1: every subscriber may publish the free allowance of comment words per month without charge.

triples.name: fee rule
triples.description: Rule 2: above the allowance the fee doubles with every doubling step of excess words, so that the affordable volume is bounded whatever the wealth of the commenter.

triples.name: sort rule
triples.description: Rule 3: readers can sort the dialogue by least attention received, next to most popular and most replies.

triples.name: reset rule
triples.description: Rule 4: the word counter is reset at the start of every month; the fee is charged per month.

triples.name: fee rule caps word count
triples.description: The exponential fee makes a monthly word volume beyond a few doubling steps unaffordable.

triples.name: wealth effect
triples.description: How much more comment volume a richer commenter can buy.

triples.name: doubling step caps wealth effect
triples.description: With an exponential fee the affordable volume grows only with the logarithm of the budget: a thousandfold budget buys about ten doubling steps.

triples.name: fee rule internalises publisher cost
triples.description: The commenter's stated goal: internalise the external cost of comment volume.

triples.name: unnoticed sort spreads attention
triples.description: Redistributes attention without forbidding anything; a lever on attention received, whereas the fee rule is a lever on volume produced.

triples.name: reset rule mirrors decay
triples.description: Answers the point that in nature and in analogue culture everything ends, while forums store everything forever.

triples.name: deliberate overuse
triples.description: Publishing many comments on purpose to make the allocation problem visible.

triples.name: self limit
triples.description: A voluntary personal cap on comment volume, set and announced by the commenter.

triples.name: overuse aims at fee rule
triples.description: Stated intent of Timon Zielonka: the high volume is meant to draw attention to the problem so that a rule follows.

triples.name: overuse enables fee rule
triples.description: Disputed claim: whether the demonstration makes the rule more likely or is read as the problem itself.

triples.name: self limit versus overuse
triples.description: The two responses to the same diagnosis exclude each other for one person at one time.

triples.description: Example: stays well inside the allowance.

triples.name: regular commenter
triples.description: Example: slightly above the allowance.

triples.name: heavy commenter
triples.description: Example: several times the allowance.

triples.name: extreme commenter
triples.description: Example: volume that only the fee rule stops.

triples.name: comment reader
triples.description: An internet user who reads comment sections.

triples.name: comment reader share
triples.description: Fraction of internet users who read comment sections.

triples.name: low adoption
triples.description: Scenario: 20 percent of internet users are on sites and services that implement the rules.

triples.name: medium adoption
triples.description: Scenario: 50 percent of internet users are on sites and services that implement the rules.

triples.name: high adoption
triples.description: Scenario: 80 percent of internet users are on sites and services that implement the rules.

triples.name: adoption share
triples.description: Fraction of internet users covered by a scenario.

triples.name: platform count
triples.description: Number of platforms that must implement the rules to reach a scenario; grows steeply because the long tail of small forums covers few users each.

triples.name: benefit per reader
triples.description: Yearly value a comment reader gains from a rule, mainly attention no longer spent on diluting volume, valued at about ten US dollars per hour.

triples.name: harm per reader
triples.description: Yearly damage a rule causes per comment reader: excluded or shortened contributions, pay-to-speak perception, visibility for spam.

triples.name: effort per platform
triples.description: Yearly cost of implementing and running a rule on one platform: counting, billing, support, dispute handling.

triples.name: net benefit
triples.description: Benefit minus effort minus harm.

triples.name: fee rule excludes
triples.description: Harm channel: commenters with low income and a volume between allowance and cap are priced out; readers may perceive the forum as pay-to-speak.

triples.name: fee rule circumvented
triples.description: Harm channel: several accounts per person, or moving the volume to non-adopting platforms; captured by leakage.

triples.name: allowance rule shortens
triples.description: Harm channel: pressure to keep contributions short even where length is warranted.

triples.name: unnoticed sort surfaces spam
triples.description: Harm channel: comments that are unnoticed for good reason gain visibility.

triples.name: reset rule bursts
triples.description: Harm channel: heavy commenters spend the fresh allowance in the first days of the month.

triples.name: affordable words
triples.description: Monthly comment words a commenter can pay for with a given budget.

formulas.name: rule benefit formula
formulas.expression: "benefit" = "internet user" * "adoption share" * "comment reader share" * "benefit per reader" * ( 1 - "leakage" )
formulas.latex: B = U \cdot s_a \cdot s_r \cdot b \cdot ( 1 - l )
formulas.description: Yearly benefit of a rule in a scenario: covered comment readers times benefit per reader, reduced by the share of the effect that leaks to non-adopting platforms.

formulas.name: rule harm formula
formulas.expression: "harm" = "internet user" * "adoption share" * "comment reader share" * "harm per reader"

formulas.name: excess words formula
formulas.description: Applies only when the word count exceeds the free allowance; otherwise the excess is zero.

formulas.name: comment fee formula
formulas.description: Exponential fee: doubles with every doubling step of excess words. The first step costs the base fee.

formulas.name: affordable words formula
formulas.expression: "affordable words" = "free allowance" + "doubling step" * log( "budget" / "base fee" + 1 ) / log( 2 )
formulas.description: Inverse of the fee formula: the monthly word volume a budget can buy grows only with the logarithm of the budget.
